relations.subject: Morinaga Sōkō
relations.evidence: Between 1986 and 1994 he was president of Hanazono University.

relations.subject: Morinaga Sōkō
relations.evidence: In 1949, he became a monk at Daishu-in under Gotō Zuigan, formerly abbot of Myōshin-ji and at that time abbot of Daitoku-ji.

relations.subject: Morinaga Sōkō
relations.evidence: he entered Daitoku-ji monastery and trained under his elder Dharma brother Oda Sessō Rōshi... Young Sōkō continued training at Daitoku-ji monastery until he received inka shōmei from Sessō Roshi in 1963.

relations.subject: Oda Sessō
relations.evidence: Oda Sessō Rōshi, who was also a disciple of Gotō Zuigan Rōshi

relations.subject: Oda Sessō
relations.evidence: Oda Sessō Rōshi, who was also a disciple of Gotō Zuigan Rōshi and who had succeeded him as abbot of Daitoku-ji.

relations.subject: Myōkyō-ni
relations.evidence: In 1984 he ordained Venerable Myōkyō-ni, head of the Zen Centre and closely affiliated to the London-based Buddhist Society.

relations.subject: Shaku Daijō
relations.evidence: He had a number of Western students, notably Shaku Daijō and Ursula Jarand, both students of many years at Daishu-in in Kyōto.
